standard_prerequisites.use: The lifting definition of formal etaleness (definition-formally-etale, same chapter) and the topological fact that a first-order thickening does not change the underlying space; cited inputs with the diagram argument written in the retained span.

core_obligations: Set up a solid lifting diagram for f|_U over a first-order thickening of T by T'.
Obtain the unique S-morphism a' : T' -> X extending a from formal ramifiedness of f.
Show a'(T') lands in U because |T'| = |T|, and conclude the unique dotted arrow for f|_U.

proof_roadmap.step: Produce the unique lift into X from formal etaleness of f.
Factor the lift through U via invariance of the underlying space.

difficulty_reason: If f : X -> S is formally etale, then the restriction f|_U : U -> V to open subschemes with f(U) contained in V is formally etale. The retained proof runs the definition: for a solid diagram with a first-order thickening i : T -> T', formal ramifiedness (uniqueness part of formal etaleness) yields a unique S-morphism a' : T' -> X extending a, and since the underlying spaces of T and T' agree, a' factors through U, giving the unique dotted arrow into U. Retained author proof at lines 1580-1592.
